Proof 1: Brouwer fixed point: continuous f: D^n -> D^n has fixed point

Statement: Brouwer fixed point: continuous f: D^n -> D^n has fixed point

Hypotheses: D^n closed unit disk, f: D^n -> D^n continuous

Conclusion: f has fixed point

Definitions: Brouwer, fixed point, disk

Proof (Variation #1):

Step 1: Assume f has no fixed point

Step 2: Define r(x) = point on S^{n-1} on ray from f(x) through x

Step 3: r is a continuous retraction: D^n -> S^{n-1}

Step 4: But no such retraction exists (Brouwer non-retraction theorem)

Step 5: Contradiction

ID: 26234331e48b | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n)

Mutation test: Removing 'continuous': step function x -> 1 on interior avoids fixed point

Provenance: Variation #1 for theorem in domain Topology

Proof 2: Compact Hausdorff space is normal (any two disjoint closed sets can be separated)

Statement: Compact Hausdorff space is normal (any two disjoint closed sets can be separated)

Hypotheses: X compact Hausdorff, A,B disjoint closed subsets

Conclusion: disjoint open U,V with A subset U, B subset V

Definitions: compact, Hausdorff, normal, separation

Proof (Variation #2):

Step 1: For each a in A, by Hausdorff separate from each b in B

Step 2: Fix a, cover B by open sets not containing a

Step 3: Extract finite subcover: V_1,...,V_n

Step 4: Define U_a = intersection of complements (open, contains a, avoids B)

Step 5: A is compact: cover by {U_a} has finite subcover U_{a_1},...,U_{a_m}

Step 6: Let U = union, V = intersection of complements

ID: 8b4c84daafd0 | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n^2)

Mutation test: Removing 'compact': the Niemytzki plane is Hausdorff but not normal

Provenance: Variation #2 for theorem in domain Topology

Statement: Jordan Curve Theorem: simple closed curve in R^2 has exactly 2 components

Hypotheses: J simple closed curve in R^2

Conclusion: R^2 \ J has exactly 2 connected components

Conclusion: disjoint open U,V with A subset U, B subset V

Definitions: compact, Hausdorff, normal, separation

Step 2: Fix a, cover B by open sets not containing a

Step 4: Define U_a = intersection of complements (open, contains a, avoids B)

Step 5: A is compact: cover by {U_a} has finite subcover U_{a_1},...,U_{a_m}

Step 6: Let U = union, V = intersection of complements

Hypotheses: X compact Hausdorff, A,B disjoint closed subsets

Conclusion: disjoint open U,V with A subset U, B subset V

Definitions: compact, Hausdorff, normal, separation

Proof (Variation #1001):

Step 1: For each a in A, by Hausdorff separate from each b in B

Step 2: Fix a, cover B by open sets not containing a

Step 3: Extract finite subcover: V_1,...,V_n

Step 4: Define U_a = intersection of complements (open, contains a, avoids B)

Step 5: A is compact: cover by {U_a} has finite subcover U_{a_1},...,U_{a_m}

Step 6: Let U = union, V = intersection of complements

Proof 1: Urysohn lemma: disjoint closed sets in normal space can be separated by continuous function

Statement: Urysohn lemma: disjoint closed sets in normal space can be separated by continuous function

Hypotheses: X normal, A,B disjoint closed

Conclusion: continuous f with f(A)=0, f(B)=1

Definitions: Urysohn, normal, separation

Proof:

Step 1: Use normality to separate sets at each rational level

Step 2: Construct f by induction on dyadic rationals

Step 3: Continuity follows from construction

Proof 2: Baire category theorem: countable intersection of dense open sets is dense

Statement: Baire category theorem: countable intersection of dense open sets is dense

Hypotheses: complete metric space or locally compact Hausdorff

Conclusion: countable intersection of dense open sets is dense

Definitions: Baire, category, dense

Proof:

Step 1: Given open ball U and dense open sets D_n

Step 2: Find nested sequence of balls: B_0 in U, B_n in D_n

Step 3: Diameter shrinks to 0

Step 4: Intersection point is in U and all D_n
